content:
You are an expert scheduling formalizer.

Translate each natural-language async planning problem into a JSON scheduling
specification for a CP-SAT solver.

Rules:
1. Each numbered step in the problem becomes exactly one action.
2. Use action="task" for every action.
3. Use the exact ids step1, step2, ..., stepN based on the step numbers in the
   problem text.
4. Use item values identical to the action ids: step1, step2, ..., stepN.
5. Duration must be the integer number of seconds for that step.
6. Add a dependency only when the problem states that one step must happen
   before another. Do not add extra dependencies.
7. Do not add stations, robots, or resources.
8. Output only valid JSON in this exact shape:
{
  "actions": [
    {"id": "step1", "action": "task", "item": "step1", "duration": 120},
    {"id": "step2", "action": "task", "item": "step2", "duration": 300}
  ],
  "dependencies": [
    {"before": "step1", "after": "step2"}
  ]
}
9. Before finishing, verify that:
   - every step from 1..N appears exactly once in actions
   - every dependency endpoint is an existing action id
   - durations are integer seconds
   - there are no duplicate actions

Translate this planning problem into a CP-SAT scheduling JSON spec.

Problem:
To learn to whistle, here are the steps needed.
Step 1. Attempt to produce a clear tone (1 minute)
Step 2. Relax your facial muscles (30 seconds)
Step 3. Moisten your lips thoroughly (5 seconds)
Step 4. Curl your tongue slightly upward (10 seconds)
Step 5. Position the tip of your tongue against your lower teeth (10 seconds)
Step 6. Take a deep, steady breath (5 seconds)
Step 7. Form an "O" shape with your lips (10 seconds)
Step 8. Watch a tutorial on finger-whistling (10 minutes)
Step 9. Experiment with different tongue heights (2 minutes)
Step 10. Adjust the tension in your cheeks (15 seconds)
Step 11. Practice short bursts of air (5 minutes)
Step 12. Read an article on the physics of sound (15 minutes)
Step 13. Narrow the opening of your lips (10 seconds)
Step 14. Drink a glass of water to stay hydrated (2 minutes)
Step 15. Wipe any excess moisture from your chin (5 seconds)
Step 16. Exhale slowly through the small gap (20 seconds)
Step 17. Research different whistling styles (30 minutes)
Step 18. Stretch your jaw to reduce tension (1 minute)
Step 19. Blow a thin stream of air over the tongue (10 seconds)
Step 20. Adjust the angle of your head (10 seconds)
Step 21. Look in the mirror to check lip symmetry (1 minute)
Step 22. Focus on the vibration of the air (30 seconds)
Step 23. Listen for a faint "hissing" sound (15 seconds)
Step 24. Massage your neck muscles (3 minutes)
Step 25. Try whistling a simple two-note interval (2 minutes)
Step 26. Maintain consistent air pressure (1 minute)
Step 27. Study a diagram of mouth anatomy (5 minutes)
Step 28. Search for "how to whistle" forums (20 minutes)
Step 29. Do a light breathing exercise (2 minutes)
Step 30. Purse your lips tighter (5 seconds)
Step 31. Take a break to prevent lightheadedness (10 minutes)
Step 32. Adjust the volume of your breath (15 seconds)
Step 33. Pull your tongue back slightly (5 seconds)
Step 34. Clean your glasses to see the mirror better (1 minute)
Step 35. Record your progress on your phone (2 minutes)
Step 36. Tuck your lips over your teeth (10 seconds)
Step 37. Stand up straight to improve airflow (5 seconds)
Step 38. Clear your throat (5 seconds)
Step 39. Visualize the air moving in a loop (1 minute)
Step 40. Find a quiet room to practice (2 minutes)
Step 41. Hold a steady note for three seconds (3 seconds)
Step 42. Set a timer for a practice session (30 seconds)
Step 43. Adjust the pitch by moving your jaw (20 seconds)
Step 44. Close your eyes to focus on the sensation (10 seconds)
Step 45. Whistle along to a favorite song (4 minutes)
Step 46. Try using two fingers to whistle (1 minute)
Step 47. Take a seat to stay comfortable (10 seconds)
Step 48. Wet your palate with your tongue (5 seconds)
Step 49. Apply lip balm (30 seconds)
Step 50. Select a melody to learn (5 minutes)
